page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors with x86_64 architecture. The server provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of memory per thread. The CPU cache architecture features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and includes no local storage out of the box, requiring remote persistent disks for persistent storage needs. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, though extended vector instructions like AVX-512 and AMX are omitted.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong overall compute and memory throughput. In stress-ng, the instance achieves top 25% performance with scores of 2,689.77 in single-core and 64,801.91 in multi-core metrics. PassMark testing further corroborates this tier with an overall CPU score of 51,859.38 and strong ratings in CPU physics (6,575.96) and cryptographic functions (51,374.99). In contrast, general integer throughput shows mid-tier figures, marked by a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 1,496.0 and multi-core score of 13,559.0.

Memory subsystems exhibit substantial throughput on larger footprints, recording 217.04 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 112.75 GB/sec for uncached writes, both falling into the top 25% tier. The PassMark memory benchmark similarly ranks in the top quartile at 2,759.14. However, small-block cached read bandwidth (3,048.86 GB/sec) and database operation throughput (19,873.74 ops/sec) remain in the middle 50% category alongside Redis SET throughput at 47.48 million ops/sec.

The server delivers balanced performance-per-resource efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or local NVMe scratch disks. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, analytical processing, enterprise application backends, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.

Reflecting an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it targets memory-heavy computing without included local disks or GPU accelerators. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (64,801.91), PassMark CPU score (51,859.38), and PassMark memory performance (2,759.14).
